Longhaul has two kinds of result. The chaos suite is measured: it shows what a crash costs a running task. The model evaluation, which shows how well the agent fixes issues and what a fix costs, is pending. The chaos chart and table on this page are read from the committed result file each time the site is built.

## The chaos suite: measured

The suite runs four recorded tasks 20 times. Each run is hit with one to three kills of four kinds: the worker process, the task's sandbox, the Temporal server and Postgres. Delivery goes to a fake GitHub that the run owns, and the suite counts the comments, labels and pull requests it finds there. It does not count them from Longhaul's own tables, because a table that decides whether a write happened cannot also be the witness.

::: {fragment="_generated/chaos-chart.md"}
:::

::: {fragment="_generated/chaos-table.md"}
:::

How to read it:

- **Completed** and **Diff equal** count the runs that a kill of that type hit. A run counts as completed when the task ended with a pull request, and as diff equal when its final diff is the diff of the same task run with no kill.
- **Duplicate side effects** are the writes on the fake GitHub beyond the ones a task makes.
- **Resume** is the time from the end of a kill to the start of the next activity, from the timestamps in Temporal's history. The worker latency is mostly the 20 second heartbeat timeout of these runs, which is how long Temporal waits before it decides the activity is dead.

Two limits go with the table. The model answers were scripted recordings, so it measures durability and says nothing about how well a model codes. And not every planned kill landed: in two runs none of them landed before the run ended, so those runs show nothing about a crash.

The method is in [`eval/chaos/README.md`]({{< meta source-repo >}}/blob/main/eval/chaos/README.md), and the numbers are in [`eval/results/chaos-2026-11-07/summary.json`]({{< meta source-repo >}}/blob/main/eval/results/chaos-2026-11-07/summary.json). `scripts/chaos_chart.py` draws the chart from that file.

## The model evaluation: pending

The resolve rate on a 40-task subset of SWE-bench Verified and on a set of 15 custom tasks, compared with a naive loop and a single-shot baseline, the dollars per resolved task, and the two ablations (compaction and memory) are not measured yet. The runs call a live model, so they need an API key, and the SWE-bench runs need the eval VM, because the harness pulls several GB of images for each task. Until those runs exist this page makes no claim about them.

These are the questions the runs answer. Each one needs a number from a recorded run before the README can claim an answer, and every result file records the config hash, the model id, the git sha and the seed. The [result tables in the plan](plan.qmd#results-table-templates-filled-only-from-result-files) stay empty until a result file fills them.

::: {fragment="_generated/eval-questions.md"}
:::

The method, the task sets, the run matrix and the formulas are in [section 8 of the plan](plan.qmd#evaluation-and-proof-plan).

## The report of the model runs

`eval/report/build_report.py` writes `docs/results.md` from the result files of the model runs, and the rest of this page is that file. Until the runs are made it holds no numbers, and it lists the commands that make them.
